text:
marco_ae: Heads-up — enterprise POC with NovaBank wants a geo-standby plan: primary EU region + hot standby in us-west. They care about data residency, sub-processors, and a clear delta on pricing for standby capacity. Can SE/infra chime in?

anya_se: Thanks Marco. Quick Qs: 1) Do we have a defined egress path when failover hits standby (i.e., will traffic traverse public internet vs peered path)? 2) Which sub-processors would process any ephemeral data in the standby region?

devon_sre: Short answers: 1) By default failover will route to the nearest compatible endpoint — that can be our peered VPC in us-west if customer has tenant peering enabled, otherwise public egress. 2) Sub-processors in standby depend on region: us-west typically hits AWS us-west-2 infra; if they use Dedicated we may involve our managed-network partner (NetCrest) for peering.

marco_ae: Customer specifically asked for no third-party transfer outside AWS/Azure for standby. They also asked for a timeline for sub-processor attestations (SOC2/ISO).

sarah_security: @marco_ae we can provide the current sub-processor roster and attestation status. For AWS/Azure we have SOC2 certs already; NetCrest has a pending ISO27001 expected in ~6 weeks. If the customer needs zero third-party, Dedicated + tenant peering is the recommended route.

anya_se: Perfect — can we also get a ballpark pricing delta for hot-standby? Sales needs an initial number today for the SOW. Simple model: warm standby keeping model weights cached and minimal serving threads vs full active cluster.

devon_sre: Ballpark: warm standby (KV warm, minimal workers) ~1.15x of normal reserved capacity. Hot standby (full ready with same throughput) ~1.4x. These are estimates — exact depends on model size and expected RPS. Also note cross-region egress will add bandwidth charges.

marco_ae: Noted. Can you sketch a minimal routing policy we could propose? Customer wants deterministic failover (no auto-fallback to other regions except us-west).

devon_sre: Sure — sample policy snippet: ```json
{
  "routing": {
    "primary": "eu-central-1",
    "standby": "us-west-2",
    "failover_mode": "manual_or_pin",
    "allow_fallback": false,
    "peering_required": true
  }
}
```

sarah_security: FYI — if allow_fallback is false we must document the SLA implications. If standby is in a different legal jurisdiction, include data flow diagrams in the security pack. I can draft the appendix.

marco_ae: Great — timeline constraints from customer: procurement needs sub-processor attestations by next Friday, and pricing for warm vs hot standby by EOD today.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline check: dedicated-network-onboarding pipeline currently estimated 3 business days once legal sign-off and peering cidr provided.

anya_se: Action items: (1) Sarah - send sub-processor roster + expected attestation dates to Marco (by EOD today). (2) Devon - update pricing delta with model-specific knobs; give low/med/high estimates (by 17:00). (3) Marco - confirm if customer will accept Dedicated+peering or insists on Hosted only.

marco_ae: I'll ping them now and get back in this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
